title: Why 12 Monkeys Deserves More Recognition
excerpt:
A retrospective revisits Terry Gilliam's 1995 science-fiction film.
Its time-travel mystery and performances remain compelling.
body_md:
Discussions of great 1990s cinema frequently revolve around Pulp Fiction and The Silence of the Lambs. A new retrospective argues that 12 Monkeys deserves a place in the same conversation.

Bruce Willis plays Cole, a prisoner sent into the past to investigate a devastating virus. The Army of the Twelve Monkeys is initially suspected, but the story challenges the reliability of the information guiding his mission.

The film's opening music establishes its unsettling atmosphere. Its time-travel framework also raises questions about memory, fate and perception rather than functioning solely as a puzzle.

Brad Pitt's energetic performance as a psychiatric patient is another highlight. The writer compares its intensity with Johnny Depp's work in Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas. The contrast with Willis's character gives the film a distinctive dynamic.

This is a critical retrospective, not an announcement of a sequel or remake.
